prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the open outdoor layout of a baseball field, showing a continuous ground plane that recedes from bright white in the immediate foreground (roughly 1 to 3 metres below and in front of the camera wearer, nothing within arm's reach) to dark grey across the grass outfield and dirt diamond (10 to 50 metres) and nearly black at the perimeter treeline, dugout building, and tall light poles (40 to 100 metres away) beneath a black sky. Across the five frames, the bright near-ground gradient shifts as the camera wearer pans right from the dirt infield (frames 1 and 2) across the open grass outfield with a slightly downward tilt that brings more near grass into view (frames 3 and 4), before turning back left toward the diamond with a slight roll tilt (frame 5). Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly isolates the thin vertical silhouettes of the stadium light poles and flagpole against the sky and shows the continuous planar slope of the turf. However, the map is unreliable on the brown dirt infield in frames 1, 2, and 5—where a sharp darker discontinuity makes the flat dirt surface appear artificially recessed relative to the bordering grass—and it fails to resolve the see-through chain-link backstop fence, distant tiny people near the backstop (roughly 35 to 50 metres away), and white fisheye border padding corners.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely black across all five frames, detecting no discrete object or person masks anywhere in the scene. Using the RGB strip for spatial context, the environment consists mainly of background stuff classes—a grass outfield, a dirt baseball diamond 10 to 40 metres ahead, a distant treeline 50 to 100 metres away, and a sky canopy above—along with static structures like tall light poles, fencing, and a small building 40 to 60 metres to the right. As the camera wearer pans right from the infield to the outfield in frames 1 through 4 and turns back left in frame 5, no people or movable objects ever enter arm's reach or the foreground. The map adds no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is unreliable for small or distant instances, completely missing the tiny figures standing near the distant backstop fence (roughly 35 to 50 metres away) as well as structural fixtures like the light poles and dugout.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is entirely black across all five frames, containing no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand keypoints. This confirms that the camera wearer's own hands and arms remain out of the field of view and that no other person is in the foreground or mid-ground within several metres of the camera wearer as the view pans right across the grass outfield (frames 1 to 4) and back left toward the baseball diamond (frame 5). Consequently, no facing directions, gaze orientations toward the camera wearer, or arm's-reach interactions can be established from skeletal geometry. While this absence of detections aligns with the empty near-field in the RGB strip, the pose estimator is unreliable at long range and fails to detect the minuscule, low-resolution silhouettes of distant people near the infield backstop roughly 35 to 50 metres away in frames 1, 2, and 5.
